docs.title: modsim
docs.text: Modsim is a Modbus simulator for local development and integration with modpoll. Its default datastore contains coils, discrete inputs, holding registers and input registers. All Unit IDs share that datastore. A public Modbus TCP simulator is available at modsim.topmaker.net:502 for quick testing.

docs.title: Run the default simulator
docs.text:
pip install modsim
modsim --comm tcp --port 5020

Alternatively, start the published container:

docker run --rm -p 5020:5020 topmaker/modsim:latest

The default TCP listener uses port 5020. Coils and holding registers are writable; discrete inputs and input registers are read-only. Unsupported addresses return a Modbus exception.

docs.title: Transports and options
docs.text:
TCP and UDP use socket framing; UDP listens on loopback. TLS uses TLS framing and expects examples/certificates/pymodbus.crt and pymodbus.key relative to the working directory. The TLS server does not authenticate clients. Serial supports RTU and ASCII framing; physical serial devices have not been validated in the local regression suite.

Only the sequential datastore is implemented. The CLI rejects non-default --store values and the unsupported --slaves and --context options. Run modsim --help for the full option list.

The local TCP, UDP and temporary-certificate TLS tests cover startup, reads and shutdown. SIGINT and SIGTERM handling on Windows has not been verified.

docs.title: Model-driven simulation
docs.text: The v2 source uses the published, exact modpoll-wot==0.2.0a1 dependency. Install with poetry install. Model parsing and TM instantiation belong to that shared package; Modsim owns state and protocol execution.

docs.title: One device
docs.text:
poetry run modsim --config contrib/advantech/adam-5017uh/adam-5017uh-slot-0.tm.json \
  --unit-id 1 --port 5020 \
  --scenario contrib/advantech/adam-5017uh/temperature.sim.json

--config also accepts HTTPS model URLs. GitHub blob links are converted to raw file URLs. Prefer a tag or commit SHA for repeatable runs; branch URLs change. Downloads have a 15-second timeout and a 1 MiB limit, and use the shared bounded JSON loader. Only models are downloaded; no script is fetched or executed from a model. JSON-LD context URLs are vocabulary identifiers, not execution sources.

The configured runtime supports profile 0.2 integer types (16/32/64-bit, signed/unsigned), IEEE float16/32/64, fixed-capacity UTF-8 strings, register and physical scalar booleans, physical boolean arrays, legacy register bool/bool8/ bool16 arrays, register bit selectors and explicit legacy-MSB packed bit payloads. Byte and word ordering follow the shared contract; legacy packed bit numeric payloads ignore word ordering, and packed strings ignore both, matching Modpoll.

Initialization, script updates, generators and Modbus writes use the same codec. Integer-wire multipliers are inverted with exact rational arithmetic: values that require fractional raw integers or overflow are rejected instead of truncated. Negative factors are supported. A zero factor can only encode engineering zero, using raw zero. IEEE values use their representable wire precision; startup reports and device.get return the decoded value. Model constraints apply after quantization too: an unrepresentable exact const is rejected. Numeric initial values use bounded candidates and arithmetic, not enumeration of 32/64-bit ranges. Complex constraints may require an explicit initial value/default/enum.

Strings must fit their UTF-8 byte capacity, use zero padding and cannot end in NUL (consumers strip trailing NULs). Physical bit arrays have their declared length. Legacy register bool arrays retain the consumer's byte/LSB layout and preserve unused padding. No engineering-unit conversion is guessed for raw ADAM channels. Profile 0.2 is required; the unconfigured demonstration is unchanged.

docs.title: Multiple devices on one listener
docs.text:
poetry run modsim --deployment examples/lab.sim.json

Deployment version "1" has one optional server object and a nonempty devices list. Server fields are comm (currently tcp), bind (default 127.0.0.1) and port (default 5020). --bind and --port override these listener settings. Each device requires unique name and unitId (1–254), plus model (local path or HTTPS URL). Optional fields: scenario, script, initial, parameters. Parameters instantiate model placeholders. A concrete TD with a conflicting Unit ID is rejected by the shared interpreter. A TD's remote endpoint never selects the listener bind address.

Deployment files are local. Relative model/scenario/script paths are resolved against the deployment directory. Script paths inside a scenario are relative to that scenario. CLI paths are relative to the working directory. Device state, script module state and random generators are independent even when the same TM is instantiated repeatedly. Duplicate names/Unit IDs, unsupported fields and invalid initial values fail before the listener opens. Unconfigured Unit IDs return an error and never inherit another device's state.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
Version "1" fields:

Field Meaning initial Property-name/value overrides tick Update interval in seconds, default 1, minimum 0.001 seed Per-instance random seed, default 0 generators Property-name to generator specification bindings Target property to source property for synthetic loopback writePolicy hold (default) or overwrite for generated properties script Local Python file parameters Script values exposed as device.parameters

Generators: constant (value); sine (center, amplitude, positive period); ramp (start, rate, minimum, maximum, clamped to bounds); noise (minimum, maximum, uniform seeded noise). Integer-property noise uses integer sampling to preserve the full 64-bit range. Numeric generators round to the nearest integer for integer model properties. Boolean channels can use constant values, bindings or scripts. All updates must satisfy the model's schema and raw encoding bounds. Unknown properties are errors. Binding chains and cycles are rejected; use a script for ordered dependencies.

Initialization order: model defaults/type fallback → scenario initial → deployment/CLI initial → script initialize → first dynamic update at elapsed 0. --initial and --initial-file remain available for single-device runs. Startup logs include the final initialized values; raw values are synthetic unless the contribution explicitly documents their source.

On each tick: generators → script tick → bindings. Modbus writes validate the whole request, then run on_write and bindings before responding. Invalid write requests or failed write hooks roll back register changes. Partial register writes re-decode every overlapping property, including properties whose first register was not touched. Batch updates and alias constraints are checked before commit. Bit-field updates preserve neighboring bits. Protocol writes may not change read-only/reserved bits; a writable bit sharing a register with read-only bits can be changed while preserving those bits. Reads that would expose a write-only field are rejected, while FC5/6 write echoes remain supported. Model read-only measurements may be changed internally but cannot be written by clients. hold stops a generator for a property after a valid client write until restart; overwrite permits the next tick to replace it. Scripts define their own write response and may deliberately overwrite values.

docs.title: Local Python behaviors
docs.text:
poetry run modsim --config contrib/advantech/adam-5017uh/adam-5017uh-slot-0.tm.json \
  --scenario contrib/advantech/adam-5017uh/scripted.sim.json --allow-scripts

Optional synchronous hooks:

def initialize(device):
    device.set("AI0_RAW", 100)


def tick(device, elapsed, dt):
    device.set("AI0_RAW", 100 + int(elapsed) % 100)


def on_write(device, changes):
    if "AO0_RAW" in changes:
        device.set("AI0_RAW", changes["AO0_RAW"])

Use get(name), set(name, value) and set_many({...}). Batch updates validate all values before changing cells. Hooks run on the server event loop and must not block; async hooks are rejected. Python is ordinary local code, enabled explicitly by --allow-scripts. Each device loads its own module instance. Runtime errors in periodic behavior stop the simulation and release its listener rather than silently serving stale values. SIGINT/SIGTERM cancel updates and close the server.

The sample loopback is an explicit synthetic assumption, not a claim that real ADAM hardware automatically connects AO to AI or DO to DI. No fault injection, recording/replay, multi-listener runtime or remote behavior execution is included.

docs.title: run_async_server(args) async
docs.text:
Run server.

Source code in modsim/main.py 
async def run_async_server(args: Any) -> Any:
    """Run server."""
    txt = f"Start ASYNC server, listening on {args.port} - {args.comm}"
    _logger.info(txt)
    server: Any
    if args.comm == "tcp":
        address: tuple[str, int] = (
            getattr(args, "bind", None)
            or ("127.0.0.1" if getattr(args, "runtimes", None) else ""),
            args.port,
        )
        server = ModbusTcpServer(
            context=args.context,
            identity=args.identity,
            address=address,
            framer=args.framer,
        )
        if hasattr(args, "runtimes"):
            from .runtime import RuntimeContext

            server.context = RuntimeContext(args.runtimes)
        tasks = []
        try:
            if not await server.listen():
                raise OSError(
                    "Could not start Modbus TCP listener on port %s" % args.port
                )
            tasks = [
                asyncio.create_task(device.run())
                for device in getattr(args, "runtimes", [])
            ]
            await asyncio.gather(server.serving, *tasks)
        finally:
            for task in tasks:
                task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
            await server.shutdown()
        return server
    elif args.comm == "udp":
        address = ("127.0.0.1", args.port)
        server = ModbusUdpServer(
            context=args.context,
            identity=args.identity,
            address=address,
            framer=args.framer,
        )
        try:
            if not await server.listen():
                raise OSError(
                    "Could not start Modbus UDP listener on port %s" % args.port
                )
            await server.serving
        finally:
            await server.shutdown()
        return server
    elif args.comm == "serial":
        await StartAsyncSerialServer(
            context=args.context,
            identity=args.identity,
            port=args.port,
            framer=args.framer,
        )
        return None
    elif args.comm == "tls":
        address = ("", args.port)
        cwd = os.getcwd().split("/")[-1]
        if cwd == "examples":
            path = "."
        elif cwd == "test":
            path = "../examples"
        else:
            path = "examples"

        # Create SSL context from cert and key files
        sslctx = ssl.create_default_context(ssl.Purpose.CLIENT_AUTH)
        sslctx.load_cert_chain(
            certfile=f"{path}/certificates/pymodbus.crt",
            keyfile=f"{path}/certificates/pymodbus.key",
        )

        server = ModbusTlsServer(
            context=args.context,
            identity=args.identity,
            address=address,
            framer=args.framer,
            sslctx=sslctx,
        )
        try:
            if not await server.listen():
                raise OSError(
                    "Could not start Modbus TLS listener on port %s" % args.port
                )
            await server.serving
        finally:
            await server.shutdown()
        return server
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown communication type: {args.comm}")

docs.title: setup_server(args)
docs.text:
Run server setup.

Source code in modsim/main.py 
def setup_server(args: Any) -> Any:
    """Run server setup."""
    # The datastores only respond to the addresses that are initialized
    # If you initialize a DataBlock to addresses of 0x00 to 0xFF, a request to
    # 0x100 will respond with an invalid address exception.
    # This is because many devices exhibit this kind of behavior (but not all)
    if getattr(args, "config", None) or getattr(args, "deployment", None):
        from .deployment import configure_devices

        args.context = configure_devices(args)
        _logger.info(
            "Model initialization: %s",
            json.dumps(args.model_initialization, sort_keys=True),
        )
    if not args.context:
        _logger.info("Create datastore")
        # build your payload
        co_builder = BinaryPayloadBuilder(byteorder=Endian.BIG, wordorder=Endian.BIG)
        # address=0, bytes=3
        for _ in range(3):
            # The bits within each byte are big-endian
            # The coils status (from the first position) = [1,0,1,0,0,0,0,1]
            co_builder.add_bits([True, False, True, False, False, False, False, True])

        hr_builder = BinaryPayloadBuilder(byteorder=Endian.BIG, wordorder=Endian.BIG)
        # address=0, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_16bit_uint(1)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_uint(2)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_uint(3)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_uint(4)
        # address=8, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_16bit_int(-1)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_int(-2)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_int(-3)
        hr_builder.add_16bit_int(-4)
        # address=16, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_32bit_uint(12345678)
        hr_builder.add_32bit_uint(12345678)
        # address=24, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_32bit_int(-12345678)
        hr_builder.add_32bit_int(-12345678)
        # address=32, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_32bit_float(12.34)
        hr_builder.add_32bit_float(-12.34)
        # address=40, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_64bit_uint(12345678900)
        # address=48, bytes=8
        hr_builder.add_64bit_int(-12345678900)
        # address=56, bytes=16
        hr_builder.add_64bit_float(123.45)
        hr_builder.add_64bit_float(-123.45)
        # address=72, bytes=?
        hr_builder.add_string("this is a string")

        # use that payload in the data store
        co_values = co_builder.to_coils()
        hr_values = hr_builder.to_registers()
        # Note: In PyModbus 3.16.1+, ModbusSequentialDataBlock uses address - 1 internally
        # to convert to SimData. To maintain address ranges, we use address + 1 here.
        # This maps Modbus addresses the same way as zero_mode=True did in older versions.
        device_context = ModbusDeviceContext(
            co=ModbusSequentialDataBlock(1, co_values),
            di=ModbusSequentialDataBlock(10001, co_values),
            ir=ModbusSequentialDataBlock(30001, hr_values),
            hr=ModbusSequentialDataBlock(40001, hr_values),
        )
        args.context = ModbusServerContext(devices=device_context, single=True)

    # initialize the server information
    # If you don't set this or any fields, they are defaulted to empty strings.
    args.identity = ModbusDeviceIdentification(
        info_name={
            "VendorName": "Pymodbus",
            "ProductCode": "PM",
            "VendorUrl": "https://github.com/riptideio/pymodbus/",
            "ProductName": "Pymodbus Server",
            "ModelName": "Pymodbus Server",
        }
    )
    return args

docs.title: Modsim 2.0.0a1 preview
docs.text:
Profile 0.2 TM/TD models now drive the simulator, using published modpoll-wot==0.2.0a1. A local deployment runs multiple isolated Unit IDs on one TCP listener. Models may be local or HTTPS URLs. Local scenarios support initial values, seeded generators and bindings; Python initialize/tick/on_write hooks require --allow-scripts.

The property codec covers integers, IEEE floats, strings, native/legacy booleans, byte/word orders, inverse multipliers and bit selectors. Partial writes validate overlapping properties and roll back on failure. Integer inverse transforms must be exact; constraints also apply after IEEE quantization.

Install: pip install modsim==2.0.0a1. Image: topmaker/modsim:2.0.0a1 (amd64/arm64). Documentation: https://top-maker.github.io/modsim/v2/. The repository and image include contrib ADAM models and examples/lab.sim.json. Models are manual-derived and synthetic-tested; no hardware certification is claimed. This preview leaves stable latest aliases unchanged.

docs.title: Preview release process
docs.text:
Stable release-please stays on main. A v2 prerelease uses a unique PEP 440 version and v2.* tag from v2, with matching pyproject and module versions. Push the candidate first and wait for all seven main CI jobs (quality, docs, five Python versions). The preview guard requires successful CI on that exact SHA and v2 ancestry before publishing.

preview.yml checks out the tag, saves original wheel/sdist artifacts, verifies installation and immutable registry hashes, publishes PyPI and a GitHub prerelease, then the explicit version Docker image and documentation under /v2/. Stable Docker and GitHub latest are not advanced. The preview Pages deployment preserves the stable documentation; stable-line Pages maintenance should retain /v2/.

Acceptance installs the published wheel with SHA verification, runs model/runtime protocol tests without application source, and checks the published container's two-device deployment. Do not mark a release accepted until all jobs pass. Record SHA/tag, run URL, registry hashes and acceptance results in the project log. Never replace tags or PyPI versions. If a later job fails, retry that failed job; if publication itself needs recovery, reuse the original saved distributions.
